name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: Hormuz shut; US blockade; IRGC claims mine hits
summary: Iran says Hormuz stays shut until its conditions are met; IRGC says two more tankers hit mines 11 Nov; US blockade holds
state: Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei denied talks with the US on 11 Nov and said Hormuz stays closed until Washington answers Tehran's conditions, which include ending the US naval blockade; Secretary of State Rubio said economic pressure meant major combat was not needed for now (Al Jazeera). The IRGC navy said on 11 Nov that two more tankers hit mines and caught fire on an unauthorised route (Tehran Times); this is not independently verified. A closed strait and continuing attacks on shipping set the Alert.
for_you: The war keeps oil and gas prices and shipping insurance costs high, which tends to feed through to fuel and energy bills. British nationals in or travelling to Iran and the Gulf states should follow FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Strait of Hormuz substantially closed and attacks on shipping continue as of 11 Nov

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Iran denies talks with US, says Hormuz will stay shut until demands are met
Tehran Times — Mines strike two tankers in Strait of Hormuz: IRGC Navy

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
